Description

Catechol-O-methyltransferase inactivates noradrenaline and adrenaline by methylating them, giving normetanephrine and metanephrine. Common variants of the COMT gene lower its activity and are linked to higher pain sensitivity, and the Val158Met variant is associated with pain in OA. In rats, inhibiting COMT raises pain through β2 and β3 adrenoceptors.

Colour

Proteins and metabolites are coloured by their contribution to pain: red for those that raise it (they excite or sensitise nociceptive neurons, or drive the inflammation that does), blue for those that relieve it, and olive for the shared signalling machinery (G proteins, RGS, adenylate cyclase, phospholipases, kinases, adaptors, second messengers, ions and nucleotides), whose effect is set by the receptor upstream. Metabolites take a lighter shade of the same colour. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block, so the same molecule can be red in one block and blue in another.

COMT is blue: by inactivating noradrenaline and adrenaline it lowers their pro-nociceptive action at β2 and β3 receptors. Noradrenaline is olive here, as its sign depends on the receptor: through spinal α2A receptors it suppresses pain, in injured tissue it can aggravate it (Pertovaara 2006). Normetanephrine, the inactive product, is olive.
